key_insight: Automated TIL scoring methods, including TRIGS and SAM-TIL, can predict response and survival in triple-negative and HER2-positive breast cancer with performance comparable to gold-standard clinical assessment.
clinical_relevance: These AI tools may help standardize tumour-infiltrating lymphocyte assessment for prognosis and response prediction, but they are not yet interchangeable with pathologist scoring.
method: Updated automated TIL pipeline to follow clinical scoring guidance (TRIGS)
Used a foundation model-based lymphocyte detector (SAM-TIL) and compared it with HoVerNet and muTILs
Benchmarked against gold-standard clinical assessment and outcomes such as pCR and event-free/overall survival
evidence_signal: In 285 PARTNER trial patients, model-to-clinician correlation was 0.59-0.69, and prognostic performance was similar across methods, with pCR AUC around 0.60-0.64 and event-free survival IBS about 0.10.
watch_item: Model detections are not interchangeable with manual scoring, so independent validation and careful workflow integration are still needed.
paper_title: Tumour region identification guided scoring (TRIGS) and foundation model-based Tumour Infiltrating Lymphocyte scoring are prognostic for pathological complete response/event free survival in the triple negative patients in the PARTNER randomized controlled trial
